newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala Corp lifts Manila share index at close.
newsitem.headline: Ayala Corp lifts Manila share index at close.

text.p: Philippine shares ended up on Friday on the back of gains in heavyweight Ayala Corp, which rose after winning a bid to privatise the Manila waterworks, traders said.
"Strong buying on Ayala Corp, a major contributor to the index, propped up the market," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
The main index closed up 4.15 points, or 0.12 percent, at 3,332.53 points, despite an overnight fall on Wall Street.
Ayala Corp's B shares started rising in early trade and ended up by 1.50 pesos, or 5.26 percent, at 30 pesos. Ayala A shares also posted a one peso gain, or 4.16 percent, at 25 pesos at close.

Another winning bidder in the waterworks privatisation, Benpres Holdings Corp, showed gains early in the session but traders said investors immediately decided to take profits and the counter ended steady at 10.50 pesos.
Traders said activity was focused on oil refiner Petron and in the banking sector, including Philippine National Bank and Metropolitan Bank.
"Banks are perceived as one of the major beneficiaries in a market boasting strong economic fundamentals," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, Diversified Securities executive vice-president.
Ruiz said the market may test its lifetime high of 3,375 points next week barring any major changes in the Dow.
